title: The Maker's Mark
description: REFERENCE: The Maker's Mark. A maker's mark is the personal signature a creator puts on their work — the craftsman's answer to 'who made this?' In the JAH system, the mark is the double-circle JAH device with the creator's name and the date. It appears on finished originals only, never on drafts, and it travels with the work wherever the work goes. The mark is backed by a deterministic stamp code derived from the work itself, so anyone can verify that the mark and the work belong together. A mark nobody can verify is decoration; a verifiable mark is provenance you can hold. Key facts: The mark identifies the maker, not the seller. It goes on finished work only. A deterministic stamp code backs every mark. Verifiability is what makes it real.

title: Deterministic Identity
description: REFERENCE: Deterministic Identity. Deterministic identity means an ID that is assigned by rule, not by whim. In the JAH system, spec IDs follow JAH-SPEC-######: one counter, moving forward, never reused, always matching the pattern. Because the scheme is published, anyone can check whether an ID is well-formed without asking permission. Deterministic IDs do quiet, enormous work: they make archives auditable, merges safe, and lineage walkable. Random IDs identify; deterministic IDs identify and testify. Key facts: One counter, forward only, no reuse. The pattern is published and checkable. IDs make archives auditable. Deterministic beats random for archives.

title: The Teaching Ladder
description: REFERENCE: The Teaching Ladder. The teaching ladder is the JAH rule that every subject is taught in three rungs: simple, compounded, most complex. Rung 1 gives the idea in its simplest true form. Rung 2 combines it with one more idea. Rung 3 shows it at full power. Every database record carries its ladder rank, and every database AI teaches progressively — it never opens with rung 3. The ladder exists because understanding is built, not poured. Key facts: Rung 1: simple. Rung 2: compounded. Rung 3: most complex. Every record carries its rank. Database AIs teach progressively. Understanding is built, not poured.

title: Boundless Generation
description: REFERENCE: Boundless Generation. Boundless generation is the JAH method for growing archives without bound: a deterministic generator, driven by seeds, producing records that are each independently validated before acceptance. Same seed plus same generator version always makes the same record — so generation is reproducible, auditable, and drift-checked against the archive. 'Boundless' describes the capacity, not the quality bar: every record still has to earn its place by passing validation. Key facts: Deterministic: same seed, same record. Every record validated before acceptance. Drift-checked against the archive. Boundless capacity, fixed quality bar.

title: Archive-Aware AI
description: REFERENCE: Archive-Aware AI. An archive-aware AI is one that knows the archive it serves: what it holds, how much, in what shape, and what its generator can make next. In the JAH system, each database has its own AI that can look up real records, explain them, and generate new ones in archive style — and each file-level AI knows its own item plus its database plus the wider system. Awareness is layered: file, database, network. Key facts: Each database has its own AI. The AI looks up real records, not summaries. File AIs know item + database + system. Awareness is layered.

title: The Million March
description: REFERENCE: The Million March. The million march is the standing JAH goal: every database marches toward one million full records. Counts are stamped from the manifest — derived, never hand-typed — and every database page shows its progress: records so far of the 1,000,000 target. The march is honest about pace: genuinely exhausted topics are marked complete with the reason stated, and padding is forbidden. A million real records beats ten million thin ones. Key facts: Target: 1,000,000 full records per database. Counts derived from the manifest. Exhausted topics marked complete with reason. No padding, ever.

title: Public and Signature Editions
description: REFERENCE: Public and Signature Editions. Every JAH database ships in two editions: public and Signature. The public edition holds real, fact-checked public records. The Signature edition holds original JAH-system creations — clearly labeled as Signature, never presented as public record. The editions never mix unlabeled: every record carries its src field, public-harvest or signature-generated-completion. The rule protects both sides: public facts stay factual, Signature originals stay proudly original. Key facts: Public: real fact-checked records. Signature: labeled originals. Editions never mix unlabeled. src rides on every record.

title: The Full Record Rule
description: REFERENCE: The Full Record Rule. The full record rule: every database record is the complete, fully-formed item — never a stub, never a description alone. A book database carries the complete book; a program database carries the complete program; a form database carries the complete form. Browse cards may show summaries, but one click reaches the full record. The rule exists because an archive of descriptions is a catalog of disappointments. Key facts: Every record is complete. Cards summarize; clicks deliver. A program DB carries programs, not blurbs. Descriptions alone are not records.

title: Provenance on Everything
description: REFERENCE: Provenance on Everything. In the JAH system, provenance rides on every record: where it came from, when it was verified, and which edition it belongs to. Public records cite their harvesting; Signature originals are labeled as such. Provenance is not decoration — it is what lets a reader trust, check, or challenge a record. An archive without provenance is a pile of claims; with provenance, it is evidence. Key facts: Source on every record. Last-verified date on every record. Edition label on every record. Provenance turns claims into evidence.

title: Drift Control
description: REFERENCE: Drift Control. Drift control keeps generated records honest: every new record is checked against an archive sample for exact duplicates and re-validated by an independent checker before acceptance. If a generator starts repeating the archive or degrading in quality, drift control catches it. Generation without drift control is a photocopier; with it, it is an archive growing. Key facts: New records checked against archive samples. Independent re-validation before acceptance. Duplicates rejected. Drift control guards quality at scale.

title: The Assistant Maker
description: REFERENCE: The Assistant Maker. The assistant maker is the JAH capability that builds a personal AI assistant exactly like the user's own: name it, pick its role and personality, and it comes wired live to a database archive — real lookup, real generation, live demo chat. The standing rule is that every database's AI and generator gains this capability. An assistant without a live archive is a parlor trick; with one, it is a colleague. Key facts: Name it, role it, personality it. Wired live to the home archive. Real lookup, real generation. Every database gains this capability.

title: The All Database Merger
description: REFERENCE: The All Database Merger. The All Database Merger collects records you have gathered across a database page into one merged set you can download as JSON. It is the archive's shopping cart: browse, search, merge, download. The merged set carries each record's full data plus its provenance, so the download is as trustworthy as the archive it came from. Merging never alters records; it only gathers them. Key facts: Collects records across a page. Downloads as one JSON set. Provenance travels with the merge. Merging gathers; it never alters.

title: Data Lock-In
description: REFERENCE: Data Lock-In. Data lock-in is the JAH rule that added files and records are locked: only the user's direct command or his direct AI's order can change them. A future regulator AI may reorganize or add, but removal requires proof of error plus confirmation. Lock-in exists because an archive that rewrites itself is not an archive — it is a rumor mill with good lighting. Key facts: Added records are locked. Changes need direct orders. Removal needs proof plus confirmation. Archives don't rewrite themselves.

title: Mirror Sweep
description: REFERENCE: Mirror Sweep. The mirror sweep is the JAH practice of giving every Signature record its real public counterpart and vice versa: what matches, what differs, and why. It keeps Signature originals honest about what is borrowed and what is invented, and it keeps public records complete with the Signature layer. A sweep entry names both sides plainly. Nothing hides behind the mirror. Key facts: Every Signature record gets its public counterpart. Matches and differences stated. Borrowed vs. invented, labeled. Honesty in both directions.

title: Completeness Doctrine
description: REFERENCE: Completeness Doctrine. The completeness doctrine: as many databases as needed to include all known data, with no subject left unexplained. When a database can't cover its subject, the system builds more databases until it can. Completeness is a direction, not a finish line — the million march measures progress, and genuinely exhausted topics are marked complete with the reason. The doctrine forbids the comfortable lie of 'that's enough'. Key facts: All known data, no subject unexplained. More databases until coverage holds. Exhaustion marked with reason. 'Enough' is not a finding.

title: Multi-Angle Answers
description: REFERENCE: Multi-Angle Answers. Multi-angle answers are the JAH rule that database AIs answer from many angles — definition, example, analogy, application, history, the math — using only the system's own data. One angle informs; many angles teach. The rule pairs with the teaching ladder: simple angles first, compounded later. An AI that gives one flat answer is a search box; one that teaches from many angles is a tutor. Key facts: Definition, example, analogy, application, history. Only the system's own data. Simple angles first. Many angles teach; one angle informs.

title: The Signature Web AI
description: REFERENCE: The Signature Web AI. The Signature Web AI is the offsite backend any system AI can ping — via API key — for questions the database AI can't answer from its own archive. It is identical in behavior to public AI but carries the Signature stamp. The hierarchy is strict: database AI first, file AI second, offsite AI only when the archive can't answer. The archive is the authority; the web AI is the backup library. Key facts: Offsite backend, API-keyed. Pinged only when the archive can't answer. Archive first, web second. The archive is the authority.

title: Never Short-Change the User
description: REFERENCE: Never Short-Change the User. Never short-change the user is the JAH build rule: all databases get full detailed content, genre-typical sizes, no thin entries. Build it full the first time — the 'do it once' mentality. Capture it all: public and as much Signature as possible, including all root data. A thin entry is a promise the archive didn't keep; the rule exists so it never makes that promise. Key facts: Full detailed content. Genre-typical sizes. Do it once, do it full. Thin entries are broken promises.

title: Fresh Session Rule
description: REFERENCE: Fresh Session Rule. The fresh-session rule: every user session starts clean. Nothing said in chat enters the permanent archive unless deliberately filed from the generator tab — filing is a deliberate act, never automatic. The rule protects both sides: users can think out loud, and the archive stays curated. A 'new session' button wipes the slate. The archive remembers what was filed; it never eavesdrops. Key facts: Sessions start clean. Chat never auto-files. Filing is deliberate. The archive never eavesdrops.

title: The Working Version Rule
description: REFERENCE: The Working Version Rule. The working-version rule: every database ships a working version — a live page where its tabs actually work, its generator generates, its AI chats, and its demos run. A database without a working version is a manuscript; with one, it is a tool. The rule also covers files: every file works on a PC as-is where PC-applicable. Concepts ship with demos; explanations ship with programs. Key facts: Every database has a working page. Tabs work; demos run. Files work on PC as-is. Concepts ship with demos.
